entrypoints.summary: The worm_hole parses an HTTP request line, URI, headers, and optional body, then forwards a serialized request to CADR address 0401 service HTTP over Chaosnet.
The supplied client sends a crafted HTTP URI containing query parameters and a Lisp expression in cmd after waiting for the CADR debug endpoint.

impact.affected_asset: The /tree/flag file in the service image, readable by group cadr.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause an HTTP request to trigger the documented stale-list path and invoke otherwise admin-only eval with an attacker-controlled expression.
impact.security_effect: Unauthorized evaluation of attacker-selected Lisp behavior and disclosure of the challenge flag.

causal_trace.summary: Remote-controlled HTTP method, URI, headers, and body are parsed by worm_hole; valid requests up to 512 bytes are serialized with CADR line terminators and written to the CADR HTTP Chaosnet service.
The organizer documents that returning a ZetaLisp &rest parameter leaves the returned value pointing to stack storage; returned list storage therefore does not remain live after the function returns.

The organizer documents that the stale tagged pointer can subsequently be confused with another list, with CADR pointer tagging restricting the confusion to list-compatible objects, and that triggering this path reaches admin-only eval functionality.
Admin eval enables attacker-selected Lisp evaluation; the supplied exploit expression opens server://tree//flag and reads a line, while the service image creates /tree/flag readable by group cadr.

failure.operation: Post-return confusion and use of a stack-backed stale &rest list to reach admin-only eval

primary_invariant.statement: A list returned from a function, including a value originating as an &rest parameter, must reference storage that remains valid after the callee returns.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The documented returned &rest value points into callee stack storage and is later capable of list-compatible reinterpretation after that storage is no longer live.

raw_refs.role: organizer root-cause writeup and challenge statement

quality.review_notes: Organizer README and supplied exploit provide strong challenge-level mechanism and intended end-to-end trigger evidence. No run result is included, so this record does not assert that the exploit executed successfully. The supplied Lisp source excerpt is insufficient to independently reconstruct the exact stale-list-to-eval dispatch, and no fixed binary or patch diff establishes an implementation-specific repair.

remediation.invariant_restored: Ensure values returned from &rest parameters do not retain pointers to dead stack storage, while preserving eval for requests that satisfy the legitimate administrator check.

target.component: CADR-hosted HTTP/admin evaluator reached through the worm_hole HTTP-to-Chaosnet frontend

oracle.expected_negative: A repair should prevent the unauthorized stale-list-to-eval path, while the supplied administrator-preservation checker still obtains hello world after it hooks check-admins to return true.
oracle.expected_positive: A reproduction environment accepting the supplied request should return the result of the supplied Lisp expression; the public client extracts the flag value from that response.
